title: Deterministic Instruction Step
statement: Let $A$ be a memory-augmented register program, fix an oracle and input, and suppose its instruction at state $l$ is the deterministic instruction $i$. For any Boolean value $\beta$, register assignment $v$, optional recorded answer $res$, and memory data $\mu$, one step of $A$ from the running configuration at $l$ with registers $v$ and answer $res$ leaves $\mu$ unchanged and agrees with one step of the deterministic program that keeps $A$'s deterministic instructions and replaces its other instructions by the answer $\beta$.
hypotheses_covered: $A$ is a memory-augmented register program; oracle and input are fixed
$l$ is a state and $i$ is an instruction, with $A(l)=i$ as a deterministic instruction
